description: Recorded content-director responses for Meridian's settlements (tasks 4.3, 4b.2), written the way the LLM would answer. Settlements are generated, so keys are pools by culture and kind (settlement/<culture>/<kind>/*), each settlement getting one by its key; {settlement}, {faction}, {people}, {culture} and {kind} are filled in by the game.

response.description: {settlement} is the seat of {faction}: a walled market town on a rise above its fields, where the reave holds court and the chapmen of three valleys meet on market day.
response.landmark: The reave's hall, its roof beams said to be cut from the Keel's own timbers.

response.description: {settlement}, seat of {faction}, grew from the oldest hold in the valley. Its streets wind up to a stone keep and a Keel shrine whose bell can be heard in every village of the reaveship.
response.landmark: The Oath Stone in the square, where every reave of {faction} has sworn.

response.description: {settlement} is a busy city and the seat of {faction}, ringed by mills on its stream. Its fair draws Hollish traders from far away, and lately a few strangers nobody admits to having invited.
response.landmark: The great mill, the largest wheel in the reaveship.

response.description: {settlement} is a market hold of {faction}: a palisade, a weekly market where the villages round about sell wool and barley, and a reave's man who keeps the peace and the tolls.
response.landmark: The market cross, its stone worn smooth by generations of haggling.

response.description: {settlement} is a hold at a river crossing, grown rich on the toll bridge; its wrights and smiths serve half the valley, and its inn is never empty on market day.
response.landmark: The toll bridge, its keeper's house built into the middle arch.

response.description: {settlement} is a hold on the old road, walled in a hurry after a raid in the reave's grandfather's time; it keeps a granary for the villages around it against the bad years.
response.landmark: The granary tower, the tallest thing for a day's walk.

response.description: {settlement} is a farming village of {faction}: a green, a shrine, a smithy and a few dozen houses among its strip fields.
response.landmark: An old yew on the green where the village meets to settle disputes.

response.description: {settlement} keeps sheep on the hills and barley in the valley, sends its tithe to {faction} and its young to the town fair, and has not changed much in three hundred years.
response.landmark: The shrine's bell, cracked in the Long Winter and never recast.

response.description: {settlement} is a village of {people} by the water, where the fishers and the farmers argue every spring about the mill weir.
response.landmark: The weir and the fish traps below it.

response.description: {settlement} sits at a crossing of two cart roads, and its inn earns more than its fields. Travellers of {faction} stop here on their way to the Moot.
response.landmark: The crossing inn, with a painted sign of the Fall over its door.

response.description: {settlement} is a steading of a few families farming a clearing at the edge of the woods, owing service to {faction}.
response.landmark: A wayside shrine with a scrap of old metal, polished smooth by hands.

response.description: {settlement} is a handful of herders' cottages on the high pasture, empty half the year when the flocks come down.
response.landmark: A drystone sheepfold older than anyone's memory.

response.description: {settlement} is a cluster of farms around a well, too small for a shrine, too stubborn to move.
response.landmark: The well, lined with stones carried up from the river.

response.description: {settlement} is the first landing site of the Meridian Venture and the heart of the Compact: habitat rings, greenhouses and fabrication halls around the landing field, home of the Board of Stewards.
response.landmark: The Venture's descent stage, kept where it landed as a monument.

response.description: {settlement} is the Compact's second city and the seat of {faction}: landing pads, hangars and the workshops that build the colony's landers and rovers.
response.landmark: The launch tower, lit all night, visible from the far side of the plains.

response.description: {settlement} is a survey outpost of {faction}: a few modules, a comms mast and a landing pad, crewed by surveyors on rotation.
response.landmark: The weather station, logging every hour since the outpost was founded.

response.description: {settlement} is a farming outpost: greenhouse domes and fields of Earth crops in tested soil, feeding the colony and testing what Meridian can grow.
response.landmark: The seed vault, cut into the ground beneath the domes.

response.description: {settlement} is a mining and power outpost of {faction}, its solar fields and drills feeding the colony's fabricators.
response.landmark: The solar field, a square kilometre of panels turning with the sun.

response.description: {settlement} is the Compact's watch post nearest the Hollish hills: a fenced compound with long-range cameras and a Contact Office annex that is not supposed to be used.
